statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116586 (GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4): parsing attacker-controlled JSON through github.com/go-jose/go-jose lets deeply nested arrays or objects exhaust Go's stack and crash the program, a denial of service. The advisory lists go-jose v4 before 4.1.5 and every go-jose v3 release up to 3.0.5; there is no fixed v3 release. The v4 fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a31af25836222f4c45d366d6e8f9b1049dd9935a (first released in v4.1.5), changes only json/scanner.go: scanner.pushParseState now fails past a nesting depth of 10000 and stateBeginValue returns that error; go-jose v3.0.5's json/scanner.go has no such limit. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4. We read every published caddy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine package repository, 23 versions from 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.9-r5 on x86_64 and aarch64, 46 packages, each matching its repository index checksum. Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/caddy, built with CGO_ENABLED=0; we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.9-r1: go-jose/v3 3.0.5; 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5: no go-jose/v3; and 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.4-r10: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 2.11.7-r0 to 2.11.7-r3: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 2.11.7-r4 to 2.11.9-r1: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 2.11.9-r2 to 2.11.9-r5: go-jose/v4 4.1.9. Every build from 2.11.4-r0 to 2.11.9-r1 links go-jose v3's JSON scanner (json.stateBeginValue), which is found in its function table, so those builds are affected whatever their go-jose/v4 version. go-jose/v4's JSON scanner is linked in every build; it carries the fix from go-jose/v4 4.1.5 on, so the v3 copy decides the range. 2.11.9-r2 is the first build without go-jose/v3: from that build DHI moves github.com/smallstep/certificates to the commit that caddy itself adopted in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8368 (v0.30.3-0.20261105213751-6d5a251fbe01), which drops go-jose/v3. A byte search of the program agrees in every build: go-jose/v3 names are present in every build before 2.11.9-r2 and absent from 2.11.9-r2 on. The same function-table reader finds cipher.unpadBuffer, (*cbcAEAD).Open and json.stateBeginValue in test programs we built with go-jose/v4 4.1.4 and go-jose/v3 3.0.5 for both architectures.

CVE-2026-116586 (GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4): parsing attacker-controlled JSON through github.com/go-jose/go-jose lets deeply nested arrays or objects exhaust Go's stack and crash the program, a denial of service. The advisory lists go-jose v4 before 4.1.5 and every go-jose v3 release up to 3.0.5; there is no fixed v3 release. The v4 fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a31af25836222f4c45d366d6e8f9b1049dd9935a, first released in v4.1.5, changes only json/scanner.go: scanner.pushParseState now fails past a nesting depth of 10000 and stateBeginValue returns that error. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4. We checked every published oauth2-proxy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 15 builds, 7.15.3-r0 to the current 7.15.6-r2, on x86_64 and aarch64 (30 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/oauth2-proxy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information shows the same go-jose modules on both architectures in every build, with no replace directive: go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 in 7.15.3-r0 to 7.15.4-r3, go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 in 7.15.5-r0 to 7.15.5-r3, go-jose/v4 v4.1.6 alone in 7.15.5-r4, and go-jose/v4 v4.1.8 alone in 7.15.6-r0 to 7.15.6-r2. The only other JOSE or JWT module in any build is github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5. The Go function table, which lists runtime.main in every build as a control, contains go-jose/v3's json.stateBeginValue in every build up to 7.15.5-r3, so the unfixed v3 JSON scanner is linked there; go-jose/v4's json.stateBeginValue is in every build, and the builds up to 7.15.4-r3 also carry the unfixed v4.1.4 scanner. From 7.15.5-r4 on, the function table holds no go-jose/v3 function and a byte search of the program finds no go-jose/v3/json. name, while the function table attributes go-jose/v4's json.stateBeginValue to v4.1.6 or later source files. The v4 fix is also visible in the binary: (*scanner).pushParseState, which the fix rewrites, is a separate function in the function table of every build with go-jose/v4 4.1.5 or later and of none with 4.1.4. The range ends at 7.15.5-r4, the first build with neither an unfixed go-jose/v4 nor go-jose/v3.

We checked every published scout-sbom-indexer package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository: 20 builds, 1.21.0-r0 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (40 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 version on both architectures in every build: v4.1.4 in 1.21.0-r0 to 1.23.1-r6, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-r8 to 1.26.0-r1, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-r2 to 1.29.0-r0, and v4.1.9 in 1.29.0-r1 to 1.30.0-r0; no build lists go-jose/v3, and no replace directive applies to go-jose/v4. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4/json.stateBeginValue, the scanner function the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control), so the parser is linked and the module version decides. In every build the function table attributes the go-jose/v4 json package's functions to source files of the go-jose/v4 version its build information names (apart from compiler-generated entries, which it lists as autogenerated): v4.1.4 in 1.23.1-r6 and every earlier build, v4.1.5 or later from 1.23.1-r8. The range ends at 1.23.1-r8, the first build with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5. The program also links github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4 and v5, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover.

CVE-2026-116586 (GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4): before 4.1.5, parsing attacker-controlled JSON through github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 lets deeply nested arrays or objects exceed Go's stack limit and crash the program. The fix in 4.1.5, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a31af25836222f4c45d366d6e8f9b1049dd9935a, adds a nesting limit to the JSON scanner in json/scanner.go (stateBeginValue and scanner.pushParseState); the commit is in v4.1.5 and not in v4.1.4. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4. Checked /usr/bin/trivy, the only program in every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12, 38 builds each on x86_64 and aarch64), each verified against the repository index checksum, reading its Go build information (go version -m) and its Go symbol table (go tool nm). Every build links the go-jose JSON scanner (its symbol table lists go-jose/v4/json.stateBeginValue). Builds up to 0.74.0-r9 are built with go-jose/v4 4.1.3 or 4.1.4, inside the affected range; 0.74.0-r10 is the first build with go-jose/v4 4.1.6, which carries the fix, and 0.74.0-r11 and 0.74.0-r12 carry it too. No build contains github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3, which the advisory also lists as affected.

Checked /usr/bin/alloy, the only program in every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 (1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16; 43 versions on amd64 and 44 on arm64, where 1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only), each verified against the repository's SHA-256 checksum, reading its Go build information (go version -m) and its Go symbol table (go tool nm). Every build links the go-jose JSON scanner (its symbol table lists go-jose/v4/json.stateBeginValue). Every build before 1.20.1-0 is built with go-jose/v4 4.1.4, inside the affected range; 1.20.1-0 and every later build are built with go-jose/v4 4.1.5 or 4.1.6, which carry the fix. go-jose/v3, which the advisory also lists (through 3.0.5), is not in the Go build information of any build, and no go-jose/v3 function is linked.

CVE-2026-116586 (GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4): parsing attacker-controlled JSON through github.com/go-jose/go-jose lets deeply nested arrays or objects exhaust Go's stack and crash the program, a denial of service. The advisory lists go-jose v4 before 4.1.5 and every go-jose v3 release up to 3.0.5; there is no fixed v3 release. The v4 fix, https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/commit/a31af25836222f4c45d366d6e8f9b1049dd9935a (first released in v4.1.5), changes only json/scanner.go: scanner.pushParseState now fails past a nesting depth of 10000 and stateBeginValue returns that error; go-jose v3.0.5's json/scanner.go has no such limit. Advisory: https://github.com/go-jose/go-jose/security/advisories/GHSA-vvm8-gf78-28g4. We read every published caddy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian package repository, 23 versions from 2.11.4-0 to 2.11.9-5 on amd64 and arm64, 46 packages, each matching its repository index checksum. Each holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/caddy, built with CGO_ENABLED=0; we read its Go build information and its Go function table (pclntab), which is present in every build (runtime.main is found in each). Go module versions by build: 2.11.4-0 to 2.11.9-1: go-jose/v3 3.0.5; 2.11.9-2 to 2.11.9-5: no go-jose/v3; and 2.11.4-0 to 2.11.4-10: go-jose/v4 4.1.4; 2.11.7-0 to 2.11.7-3: go-jose/v4 4.1.5; 2.11.7-4 to 2.11.9-1: go-jose/v4 4.1.6; 2.11.9-2 to 2.11.9-5: go-jose/v4 4.1.9. Every build from 2.11.4-0 to 2.11.9-1 links go-jose v3's JSON scanner (json.stateBeginValue), which is found in its function table, so those builds are affected whatever their go-jose/v4 version. go-jose/v4's JSON scanner is linked in every build; it carries the fix from go-jose/v4 4.1.5 on, so the v3 copy decides the range. 2.11.9-2 is the first build without go-jose/v3: from that build DHI moves github.com/smallstep/certificates to the commit that caddy itself adopted in https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8368 (v0.30.3-0.20261105213751-6d5a251fbe01), which drops go-jose/v3. A byte search of the program agrees in every build: go-jose/v3 names are present in every build before 2.11.9-2 and absent from 2.11.9-2 on. The same function-table reader finds cipher.unpadBuffer, (*cbcAEAD).Open and json.stateBeginValue in test programs we built with go-jose/v4 4.1.4 and go-jose/v3 3.0.5 for both architectures.

The v4 fix is also visible in the binary: (*scanner).pushParseState, which the fix rewrites, is a separate function in the function table of every build with go-jose/v4 4.1.5 or later and of none with 4.1.4. We checked every published scout-cli-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 24 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (48 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/docker-scout, a Go program with no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies. Its Go build information shows the same github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 version on both architectures in every build: v4.1.4 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-7, v4.1.5 in 1.23.1-8 to 1.26.0-2, v4.1.6 in 1.26.0-3, and v4.1.9 in 1.26.0-4 to 1.30.0-0; no build lists go-jose/v3, and no replace directive applies to go-jose/v4. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4/json.stateBeginValue, the scanner function the fix changes, in every build (runtime.main found in the same scan as a control), so the parser is linked and the module version decides. In every build the function table attributes the go-jose/v4 json package's functions to source files of the go-jose/v4 version its build information names (apart from compiler-generated entries, which it lists as autogenerated): v4.1.4 in 1.23.1-7 and every earlier build, v4.1.5 or later from 1.23.1-8. The range ends at 1.23.1-8, the first build with go-jose/v4 v4.1.5. The program also links github.com/lestrrat-go/jwx/v3 and github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4 and v5, separate JOSE and JWT libraries that this advisory does not cover. The docker-cli-scout-cli packages built from the same source hold no program code: each of the 24 published docker-cli-scout-cli builds for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64 and checked against its index checksum, contains only a symbolic link, /usr/local/libexec/docker/cli-plugins/docker-scout, pointing to /usr/bin/docker-scout.
